changes: Same engine as v3 (map SVG transform cache, frame dedup, preview-rt). This is a re-run of the same 9 renders on the quiet machine after the VM restart (load ~1-3), for a clean before/after comparison against v1. The v3 rows were measured under load 13-21 and are load-confounded.
machine: Linux VM, 7.7 GB RAM, 4 cores. QUIET after a VM restart (load ~1-3 at render start). Times are wall seconds on this machine.

determinism.map_sample_final_run_a_vs_run_b: Byte-identical video sha256 58b4d35b126b899a (v3 run-a under load 17, run-b on the quiet machine, 65.2s) and all 240 frame hashes identical. New path with map cache + dedup.
determinism.v3_vs_v3q_all_9: All 9 scene/profile videos are byte-identical between the loaded v3 runs (load 13-21) and these quiet v3q runs (load 2-9): same sha256 for every pair. Output does not depend on machine load.

preview_rt.note: Real-time preview works end to end (valid 240-frame 1920x1080 h264, all seeks reached, labelled non-deterministic) but does NOT hit the under-20s target on the loaded VM: 228.3s (v1 sampling) and 185.5s (v2 per-seek sampling) for a 10s scene-min clip. Cause: each seek waits on 2 rAF ticks and the compositor runs at ~1fps under load, so a seek takes ~0.9s vs the 41.7ms frame interval. Two preview runs give different video shas (c5404e2a vs c8296f73), as expected for a non-deterministic mode. Sampling bug found and fixed: v1 sampled the first 10s of screencast time, so the video was nearly static (inter-frame SSIM 0.9966-0.9992); v2 samples per seek, so the video shows the whole scene (inter-frame SSIM 0.9535).

quality_old_vs_new_map_sample.draft_same_profile: Old draft (sha 4ec4448e) vs new draft (sha 46c44950): 240 frames, SSIM mean 0.99997, min 0.99989, 0 frames below 0.99, PSNR mean 68.61 dB, min 52.07 dB. Profile unchanged, so this isolates the cache + dedup effect.
quality_old_vs_new_map_sample.final_profile_changed: Old final (sha 4db79517, supersample 2, preset slow) vs new final (sha 58b4d35b, supersample 1.5, preset medium): 240 frames, SSIM mean 0.99999, min 0.99996, 0 frames below 0.99, PSNR mean 72.2 dB, min 56.84 dB. Confounded by the profile change, but the pixels are still essentially identical.

tradeoffs: Preview-rt misses the under-20s target on the loaded VM (185-228s for a 10s clip). The seek/compositor rate under load is the bottleneck, not the preview design.
Map cache is not byte-identical to the legacy path (SSIM 0.998-0.99999, PSNR 44-72 dB, but a different video sha). Two runs of the same (new) path are byte-identical; only old-vs-new differs.
Wall time is dominated by machine load: map-sample final took 603.8s at load 17 and 57.0s at load 4.8, same bytes out. Every wall number must be read with its load_avg_1m.

Final is still over the 40s target for map (57.0s) and scene-min (51.1s) on the quiet machine; only text-sample final (37.5s) is under 40s. Final is 1.65x draft for map and 1.79x for scene-min (target 1.5x); text is 1.49x.
First-frame cost: the map cache adds ~0.5s at compile time (map-sample compile 0.61-0.63s steady vs 0.10-0.12s for scene-min with no map).

The SVG transform cache alone does not speed up capture (12-frame moving-camera smoke: 170s on vs 139s off, inside load noise). The measured speedup comes from frame dedup plus the profile change. A bitmap layer cache is the next step if more speed is needed.
verdict: FASTER with a named tradeoff. Quiet-machine renders are 2.5-4.8x faster than v1 (draft profiles, unchanged, are 2.5-3.1x faster from cache + dedup alone), determinism is proven byte-identical, and old-vs-new pixels match at SSIM 0.99997-0.99999. Tradeoffs: the real-time preview does not hit under-20s on the loaded VM (185-228s), and the map cache is not byte-identical to the legacy path (SSIM 0.998+, but a different video sha).
tool: headless-motion-engine (HyperFrames 0.9.20, GSAP 3.15.0, Node >= 20) with layer cache (map SVG transform cache + frame dedup) and real-time preview
